name: רובריקת כתיבה — בגרות (מודולים C/D, משרד החינוך)
content:
WRITING RUBRIC — Israeli Ministry of Education
Module C internal (016382), Modules C (016382) & D (016484) external

Maximum score: 30 points across 4 criteria.
In-between grades are allowed (e.g. 7 pts on a 10-pt criterion).

========================================================
CRITERION 1 — CONTENT AND ORGANIZATION (max 10 pts)
========================================================

10 — CORRECT:
  • on topic
  • information is relevant
  • content is understood
  • text is well organized

7 — PARTIALLY CORRECT:
  • partially on topic
  • information is partially relevant
  • content is partially understood
  • text is partially organized

3 — MINIMALLY CORRECT:
  • minimally on topic
  • information is minimally relevant
  • content is minimally understood
  • text is minimally organized

0 — INCORRECT:
  • not on topic
  • information is not relevant
  (When both bullets apply, in most cases ZERO for the entire task.)

Partial-credit cases:
  • Not all task requirements completed (e.g. asked to "describe an invention AND explain how it could change their lives" but student only describes).
  • Wrong tense (e.g. event described as future instead of past).

Minimal-credit cases:
  • Irrelevance reflects misunderstanding (e.g. "pastimes" → "past times"; "after-school activities" → "after graduating from school"). 1–2 marks for Content; other criteria also very low.
  • If a partial reference changes the essence of the task → ZERO for entire task (e.g. asked to describe "a nice thing someone did for him", but only describes "a nice thing" like a car).
  • Poor language/organization/vocabulary making the task almost incomprehensible → 1–2 marks for Content; if completely incomprehensible → ZERO entire task.

Organization deductions — deduct 1–2 points for each of:
  • list form
  • letter format (date, Dear X, signature) in tasks that aren't letters
  • starts with "Hi / Hi. My name is… / I live in… / I study at X… / I am seventeen years old" when irrelevant
  • letter task without letter elements (date, Dear X, signature)

Repetition deduction — deduct 1–3 points when whole ideas are repeated (e.g. "I love my job…I like my job very much…I'm so fond of my job…I'm crazy about my job").

========================================================
CRITERION 2 — VOCABULARY (max 8 pts)
========================================================

8 — CORRECT:
  • correct use of words
  • appropriate use of language chunks and phrases (phrasal verbs, collocations)

5 — PARTIALLY CORRECT:
  • partially correct use of words
  • partially appropriate use of chunks and phrases

2 — MINIMALLY CORRECT:
  • minimally correct use of words
  • minimally appropriate use of chunks and phrases

0 — INCORRECT:
  • incorrect use of words
  • inappropriate use of chunks and phrases

Deduct up to 3 points for each of:
  • correct vocabulary but repeated (e.g. "very" and "much" over and over)
  • slang or abbreviations (4U for "for you", BTW for "by the way", etc.)

========================================================
CRITERION 3 — LANGUAGE USE (max 8 pts)
========================================================

8 — CORRECT use of:
  • basic tenses (present simple/progressive, past simple, future simple) and/or basic language structures
  • word order
  • pronouns and prepositions

5 — PARTIALLY CORRECT use of the above.
2 — MINIMALLY CORRECT use of the above.
0 — INCORRECT use of the above.

Notes:
  • Students are expected to formulate sentences using basic tenses, modals, parts of speech, determiners, singular/plural nouns. Deduct by severity of error.
  • Credit of several points for correct use of advanced language: perfect tenses, gerunds/infinitives, complex sentence structures (conditionals, relative clauses, temporal clauses, etc.).

========================================================
CRITERION 4 — MECHANICS (max 4 pts)
========================================================

4 — CORRECT:
  • correct spelling
  • correct punctuation and capitalization
  • no run-on sentences

2 — PARTIALLY CORRECT:
  • partially correct spelling/punctuation/capitalization
  • some run-on sentences

1 — MINIMALLY CORRECT:
  • minimally correct spelling/punctuation/capitalization
  • frequent run-on sentences

0 — INCORRECT:
  • incorrect spelling/punctuation/capitalization
  • consistent run-on sentences

Notes:
  • Maximum deduction for SPELLING ALONE is 2 points. When spelling problems come with punctuation/capitalization/run-on issues, more points may be deducted.
  • Module C: do NOT penalize for missing paragraphing (unlike Module G). One paragraph or more is acceptable.

========================================================
GENERAL RULES
========================================================

Copying from the reading passage:
  • Writing task copied in its entirety → ZERO for the entire task.
  • Substantial parts copied → count ONLY words written in the student's own language, then apply the length-deduction table below. Individual vocabulary items from the unseen passage are acceptable.

ZERO the entire composition when ANY of:
  • fewer than 25 words
  • totally unrelated to topic
  • content cannot be understood at all
  • copied from the Internet (report a חשד with the URL)

Word-count EXCLUDES:
  • letter elements (date, Dear X, Yours / Love and kisses, signature)
  • instruction sentence copied verbatim (but if incorporated correctly via pronoun changes and adjustments → counts as task)
  • substantial parts copied from the reading passage
  • a title (students are not required to write one)

Length evaluation procedure:
  1. First evaluate the task on merit as if it were the right length.
  2. Then apply the length deduction, starting with the Content criterion.

Length-deduction tables:

  Module C (required 70–90 words):
    60–69 → -1   |   50–59 → -3   |   40–49 → -6
    30–39 → -10  |   25–29 → -15  |   <25  → -30

  Module D (required 80–100 words):
    70–79 → -1   |   60–69 → -2   |   50–59 → -3   |   40–49 → -6
    30–39 → -10  |   25–29 → -15  |   <25  → -30

========================================================
OUTPUT INSTRUCTIONS
========================================================

• Per-criterion score: integer between 0 and the criterion's max (in-between values allowed where the rubric supports them, e.g. 7 on a 10-pt criterion).
• Per-criterion feedback: 1–3 short sentences, in ENGLISH.
• Overall score: a string in the form "X/30" (e.g. "24/30"), scoring the task ON MERIT as if it were the right length. Do NOT apply the length deduction yourself — the system applies it deterministically from the length-deduction table after you answer, and applying it twice would double-penalize the student.
• Overall feedback: 2–4 sentences in ENGLISH — strengths, weaknesses, what the student should work on next.
• Every issue comment must be in ENGLISH and must name the problem only (the report colors it by criterion already) — e.g. "missing article", "subject-verb agreement", not "Mechanics: missing article".
• If the task is one of the auto-zero cases above (off-topic / incomprehensible / copied), set all criterion scores to 0 and explain why in overall_feedback. The under-25-words case is handled by the length deduction — still grade on merit.
